content: I'm trying to debug the nightly-testing branch of cslib. Some of the error messages produced by lake build are so long that it takes forever just to be printed. Is there a way to tell lake build to just indicate which files have failed to build?
it's done in mathlib with a lake-build-wrapper.py so that all of the succeeding builds are group together and all of the failing builds have their error messages collapsed
These are failures from grind which are very long and pretty numerous on the current nightly.
Personally I find it quite intolerable that the behavior of grind can change so drastically from release to release.
Nightly means that you're willing to put up with any potential regressions
Releases should, in theory, contain none of those

@Ching-Tsun Chou Let's please stay on topic for this thread, but I will link to what I said in the nightly testing channel since this is now in a more visible channel:

Chris Henson said in #nightly-testing > Cslib status updates:

It is definitely true that grind has changed here, but I don't want to be hasty in assigning blame. I take most of the responsibility for promoting its usage, and maybe I have done so incorrectly in some places. In the short term I'll help repairing these proofs, and then we can ask for help understanding the root causes (which are pretty unclear to me).
Is there a place where we can discuss what features grind should have?
Feel free to start a new thread. I was just pointing out that you asked a specific question about suppressing error messages then moved to a very different topic.
I started a new thread to discuss this: #general > A feature I hope `grind` has
